items.opening_verbatim: IB One Hundred Nineteenth Congress of the United States of America At the Second Session Begun and held at the City of Washington on Saturday, the third day of January, two thousand and twenty-six H. R. 2302 AN ACT To take certain Federal l
items.summary: H.R. 2302 (Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians Land Transfer Act of 2025) revokes Public Land Order 3309 and directs the Secretary of the Interior to place approximately 80 acres of BLM land and approximately 185 acres of Indian Creek Ranch land into trust for the Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians within 180 days of enactment, subject to valid existing rights. The Act directs a review to determine whether a survey is required, declares the trust land part of the Tribe's reservation, and provides that it may not be used for class II or class III gaming under the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act.
items.title: HR 2302 ENR: Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians Land Transfer Act of 2025

items.summary: H.R. 2306 (Adams Memorial-Great American Heroes Act), as reported in the Senate by Mr. Lee with an amendment on November 12, 2026, amends section 2406(l) of Public Law 116-9 and Public Law 107-62 to extend the authority of the Adams Memorial Commission through 2033. The reported text locates the Adams Memorial within the area depicted as 'Adams Memorial: Eligible Additional Area' on a map dated February 25, 2025, and requires that the final design be approved by a majority of the Commission, including specified appointed members, before it is authorized. The amendment also repeals Sections 2 and 3 of Public Law 107-315.
items.title: 107 HR 2306 RS: Adams Memorial-Great American Heroes Act

items.opening_verbatim: I One Hundred Nineteenth Congress of the United States of America At the Second Session Begun and held at the City of Washington on Saturday, the third day of January, two thousand and twenty-six H. R. 2400 AN ACT To take certain Federal la
items.summary: H.R. 2400 (Pit River Land Transfer Act of 2026) directs the Secretary of Agriculture to transfer administrative jurisdiction over approximately 557 acres of Forest Service land, known as the Four Corners Federal land, to the Secretary of the Interior, and directs that the land be taken into trust for the Pit River Tribe, subject to valid existing rights. The Act excludes approximately 87 acres of roads, highways, rights-of-way, easements, and special use permit areas, requires a complete survey within 180 days of enactment, and declares the land part of the Tribe's reservation. The land may not be used for class II or class III gaming under the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act.
items.title: HR 2400 ENR: Pit River Land Transfer Act of 2026

items.summary: H.R. 2876 (University of Utah Research Park Act) passed the House of Representatives on December 15, 2025, and was received in the Senate and placed on the calendar on November 16, 2026. The bill confirms that the University of Utah's use of approximately 593.54 acres of non-Federal land in Salt Lake City, conveyed under the Recreation and Public Purposes Act by patent 43-99-0012, as a university research park is a valid public purpose, subject to the terms of the 1970 Department of the Interior letter and related approvals. It also confirms as valid public purposes other uses consistent with a research park and related university purposes, including student housing and a transit hub.
items.title: 119 HR 2876 PCS: University of Utah Research Park Act

items.opening_verbatim: I One Hundred Nineteenth Congress of the United States of America At the Second Session Begun and held at the City of Washington on Saturday, the third day of January, two thousand and twenty-six H. R. 7834 AN ACT To limit liability for cer
items.summary: H.R. 7834 (Safe Cloud Storage Act) adds section 202 to Title II of the PROTECT Our Children Act of 2008, limiting civil claims and criminal charges against approved cloud service providers that store child pornography, child obscenity, or intimate visual depictions of minors under contracts with law enforcement or prosecutorial agencies, except in cases of specified intentional, negligent, or otherwise defined misconduct. The section sets requirements for approved vendors, including security consistent with the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, annual independent audits under NIST Special Publication 800-53 Revision 5, data stored in the United States unless the contracting agency consents to transfer, and a notification letter to the Department of Justice. The Act also specifies evidence retention rules for covered agencies and adds a clerical amendment to the Act's table of contents.
items.title: HR 7834 ENR: Safe Cloud Storage Act

items.summary: The AI Workforce Assessment and Research Enhancement Act, or the AWARE Act, as reported with an amendment in the House, amends the Act of March 4, 1913 (29 U.S.C. 2) to require the Bureau of Labor Statistics to collect full and complete statistics on the usage of artificial intelligence in conditions of labor and in products and distribution. Collection must begin no later than 18 months after enactment, and artificial intelligence is defined by reference to section 5002 of the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020. The bill's findings state that existing Bureau of Labor Statistics programs were not designed to measure employer adoption of AI, worker-level use, or related workforce effects on a timely basis.
items.title: 119 HR 9381 RH: AI Workforce Assessment and Research Enhancement Act

items.summary: The Alex Gate Safety Act of 2026, as reported by the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation with an amendment, directs the Consumer Product Safety Commission to promulgate within 180 days of enactment final consumer product safety standards consisting of ASTM F900–25, ASTM F1184–23e1, and ASTM F2200–24 as in effect on the date of enactment. It requires organizations that revise those standards to notify the Commission, with revisions treated as Commission-adopted standards after 180 days unless the Commission determines within 90 days that the revision does not improve safety. The bill also directs the Commission to conduct a national public awareness campaign within 2 years of enactment and to submit a report to Congress within 3 years.
items.title: 119 S1682 RS: Alex Gate Safety Act of 2025

items.opening_verbatim: II Calendar No. 720 119th CONGRESS 2d Session S. 1885 [Report No. 119–164] IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES May 22, 2025 Mrs. Britt (for herself, Mr. Fetterman , Mr. Husted , Ms. Slotkin , and Ms. Hassan ) introduced the following bill; w
items.summary: The Stop the Scroll Act, as reported by the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation with an amendment, requires the Federal Trade Commission, with the concurrence of the Secretary of Health and Human Services acting through the Surgeon General, to implement a mental health warning label on covered platforms, defined to include social media platforms and anonymous content sharing platforms. Under the bill, a covered label must be displayed each time a user accesses a covered platform from within the United States, must warn of potential negative mental health impacts, must provide access to federal resources including the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, and must be redisplayed after each hour of continued use. The bill directs the Commission to promulgate implementing regulations within 180 days, authorizes enforcement by the Commission and by state attorneys general, and the source text provided is truncated.
items.title: 119 S1885 RS: Stop the Scroll Act

The section designates the Institute as the primary laboratory for the executive branch on radio frequency emissions, spectrum propagation, and Federal and non-Federal spectrum sharing, and transfers the emergency communication and tracking technologies research initiative from the National Institute of Standards and Technology to the Institute. items.summary: In a dismissal decision filed September 16, 2026 and reissued for public availability November 13, 2026, Special Master Herbrina D.S. Young dismissed the petition of Kathie Wells, filed on behalf of her minor child C.B. under the National Vaccine Injury Compensation Program. The petition alleged injuries following MMR and Tdap vaccines administered October 6, 2023. The special master found that the petitioner did not file an expert report or a substitution of counsel by the court-ordered deadline, and that the medical records were insufficient to prove the claim, so the case was dismissed for failure to prosecute and for insufficient proof.

items.summary: In an opinion dated November 16, 2026, Judge Gary S. Katzmann of the U.S. Court of International Trade denied the Motion for Judgment on the Agency Record filed by Kaptan Demir Celik Endustrisi ve Ticaret A.S. and the related motion filed by plaintiff-intervenors Colakoglu. The court held that the Department of Commerce's selection of a land valuation benchmark, a Colliers International report rather than a Cushman & Wakefield report, is supported by substantial evidence. The case concerns Commerce's administrative review of the countervailing duty order on Turkish rebar for the 2022 period of review, in which the value of a rent-free government land lease was determined.

items.summary: In a non-precedential opinion in No. 25-3175, the Third Circuit affirmed a 262-month sentence imposed on Ivan Nicholas Baez for sexual exploitation of a minor. The court held that Pennsylvania harassment convictions were not similar to disorderly conduct or disturbing the peace under U.S.S.G. § 4A1.2(c), so the district court properly assigned criminal history points for them. items.summary: In a non-precedential per curiam opinion in No. 26-1765, the Third Circuit denied a pro se petition for review filed by Mamdouh Hebishy, an Egyptian citizen challenging the Board of Immigration Appeals' denial of his third motion to reopen. items.summary: In this published opinion filed November 17, 2026, the United States Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit, in an opinion by Judge Phillips, affirmed a 70-month sentence imposed by the District of New Mexico on Daniel Jesus Trujillo for illegal reentry under 8 U.S.C. § 1326. The court held that the 10-level enhancement under U.S.S.G. § 2L1.2(b)(2)(A) applies because the maximum 15-year sentence for a prior New Mexico armed-robbery conviction, minus suspended time, exceeded five years, even though actual incarceration was less than five years and New Mexico probation credit is not incarceration time. The opinion explains the guideline definitions of "sentence imposed" and "sentence of imprisonment" in §§ 2L1.2 and 4A1.2 and the procedural history of the sentencing.

items.summary: In Nealy v. Phelan, the D.C. Circuit affirmed a district court judgment upholding a Navy disability rating assigned to Navy veteran Sean Nealy, who has post-traumatic stress disorder. The Physical Disability Board of Review had recommended a six-month temporary fifty-percent rating followed by a permanent ten-percent rating, and the court found that the Navy lawfully and reasonably applied the relevant statute. The opinion was argued September 8, 2026 and decided November 17, 2026.

items.summary: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit issued an unpublished per curiam judgment on November 17, 2026, affirming the district court's dismissal of Western Towboat Company's suit against the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) and the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). The court held that NOAA's charging decision and its referral of the matter to an EPA administrative law judge are not final agency action reviewable under the Administrative Procedure Act, and that the due process claim rests on speculative future injury. The case arose from a steel drydock that capsized and sank in the Monterey Bay National Marine Sanctuary while being transported by Western, for which NOAA charged Western alone under the National Marine Sanctuaries Act after its co-respondents settled.

items.opening_verbatim: Public Law 119–139: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to conform to the intent of the Internal Revenue Service Restructuring and Reform Act of 1998, as set forth in the joint explanatory statement of the committee of conference acc
items.summary: Public Law 119–139 (H.R. 997, National Taxpayer Advocate Enhancement Act of 2025), approved November 10, 2026, amends section 7803(c)(2)(D)(i) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to authorize the Office of the Taxpayer Advocate to appoint counsel who report directly to the National Taxpayer Advocate or a delegate. A conforming amendment replaces references to local taxpayer advocate office employees with references to employees of the Office of the Taxpayer Advocate. The amendments take effect as if included in section 1102 of the Internal Revenue Service Restructuring and Reform Act of 1998.
items.title: Public Law 119–139: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to conform to the intent of the Internal Revenue Service Restructuring and Reform Act of 1998, as set forth in the joint explanatory statement of the committee of conference accompanying Conference Report 105–599, that the National Taxpayer Advocate be able to hire and consult counsel as appropriate.

items.opening_verbatim: Public Law 119–140: To amend title XVIII of the Social Security Act to clarify payment rules for manual wheelchairs under part B of the Medicare program. Public Law 140 Public Law 119–140 140 Stat. 1108 2026-11-10 2026-11-10 United States G
items.summary: Public Law 119–140 (H.R. 1703, Choices for Increased Mobility Act of 2026), approved November 10, 2026, adds paragraph (24) to section 1834(a) of the Social Security Act concerning manual wheelchairs under Medicare Part B. For ultralightweight manual wheelchairs furnished on or after January 1, 2028, the Secretary must establish two or more HCPCS codes distinguishing bases made with titanium or carbon fiber from bases made without those materials. For titanium or carbon fiber based wheelchairs, payment to the supplier follows the usual amount under the subsection, the supplier may charge the beneficiary the difference between its actual charge and that payment, and the Secretary may require the supplier to issue a notice before purchase or rental.
items.title: Public Law 119–140: To amend title XVIII of the Social Security Act to clarify payment rules for manual wheelchairs under part B of the Medicare program.

items.opening_verbatim: Public Law 119–141: To designate the America’s National Churchill Museum National Historic Landmark, and for other purposes. Public Law 141 Public Law 119–141 140 Stat. 1110 2026-11-10 2026-11-10 United States Government Publishing Office N
items.summary: Public Law 119–141 (H.R. 1945, America’s National Churchill Museum National Historic Landmark Act), approved November 10, 2026, designates the America’s National Churchill Museum National Historic Landmark, located at Westminster College in Fulton, Missouri, including the Winston Churchill Memorial. The Act authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to enter into cooperative agreements and to provide technical and financial assistance for protecting resources and providing educational and interpretive programs. It also directs the Secretary to conduct a special resource study of the site and submit a report to the Senate and House committees within 3 years after study funds are first made available.
items.title: Public Law 119–141: To designate the America’s National Churchill Museum National Historic Landmark, and for other purposes.

items.opening_verbatim: Public Law 119–142: To amend title 11, United States Code, to modify certain bankruptcy eligibility requirements, and for other purposes. Public Law 142 Public Law 119–142 140 Stat. 1112 2026-11-10 2026-11-10 United States Government Publis
items.summary: Public Law 119–142 (H.R. 7730 / S. 3977, Bankruptcy Threshold Adjustment Act), approved November 10, 2026, amends section 1182(1) of title 11, United States Code, to set the small business debtor limit at aggregate noncontingent liquidated debts of not more than $7,500,000, excluding debts owed to affiliates or insiders, with at least 50 percent arising from commercial or business activities. It excludes affiliated debtor groups above that limit, corporations subject to Securities Exchange Act reporting requirements, and their affiliates. It also amends section 109(e) of title 11 to set the chapter 13 individual debt limit at less than $2,750,000 and applies to cases commenced on or after the date of enactment.
items.title: Public Law 119–142: To amend title 11, United States Code, to modify certain bankruptcy eligibility requirements, and for other purposes.

DON YOUNG DOUG LaMALFA INDIAN BUFFALO MANAGEMENT ACT

  Mr. WESTERMAN. Mr. Speaker, I move to suspend the rules and pass the
bill (H.R. 7954) to assist Tribal governments in the management of
buffalo and buffalo habitat and the re
items.summary: The House considered H.R. 7954, the Don Young Doug LaMalfa Indian Buffalo Management Act, under suspension of the rules. The bill directs the Secretary of the Interior to work with Indian Tribes and Tribal organizations on buffalo and buffalo habitat through contracts, grants, and technical assistance, authorizes agreements to transfer surplus buffalo from Federal land to Indian land, and requires the Secretary to protect culturally sensitive or confidential tribal information. The authority provided by the bill ceases to be effective 7 years after enactment.
items.title: DON YOUNG DOUG LaMALFA INDIAN BUFFALO MANAGEMENT ACT

items.opening_verbatim:
RESPONSIBLE CORMORANT MANAGEMENT AND CONTROL ACT OF 2026

  Mr. WESTERMAN. Mr. Speaker, I move to suspend the rules and pass the
bill (H.R. 8195) to require the Secretary of the Interior to develop
regional management frameworks for
items.summary: The House considered H.R. 8195, the Responsible Cormorant Management and Control Act of 2026, under suspension of the rules. The bill directs the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, to issue regulations establishing regional management frameworks for double-crested cormorants in coordination with the four Regional Flyway Councils. The bill requires population surveys and framework updates every 5 years, annual public reporting of take, and has no force or effect beginning January 1, 2034.
items.title: RESPONSIBLE CORMORANT MANAGEMENT AND CONTROL ACT OF 2026

  The PRESIDING OFFICER. Under the previous order, the Senate will

items.summary: The Senate resumed consideration of H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, a reconciliation bill, with the pending Thune (for Graham) amendment No. 2360 in the nature of a substitute and a Schumer motion to appeal the Chair's ruling on a point of order under section 313(b)(1)(E) of the Congressional Budget Act. Senator Schumer stated that the bill would reduce Medicaid and SNAP benefits, raise electricity costs, and increase the federal debt, and announced that Democratic senators would offer amendments during the vote-a-rama. Senator Thune stated that extending the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act provisions would prevent tax increases for families earning less than $400,000 and for pass-through businesses, and cited Congressional Budget Office revenue estimates for that act.

items.summary: SA 2704, submitted by Ms. Ernst for herself, Mr. Grassley, Ms. Murkowski, and Ms. Collins, would strike sections 70512 and 70513 of H.R. 1 and insert new provisions on the clean electricity production credit. For wind and solar facilities, it sets a phase-out percentage that multiplies the credit: 60 percent for facilities whose construction begins in 2026, 20 percent for those beginning in 2027, and 0 percent for those beginning after December 31, 2027. It also restricts the credit for facilities using material assistance from prohibited foreign entities and adds definitions of specified foreign entities and foreign-influenced entities to section 7701(a), and the text is truncated before its end.

items.summary: Senator Lee submitted amendment SA 2724 to H.R. 1, which was ordered to lie on the table. The amendment would add the Regulations from the Executive in Need of Scrutiny Act of 2025 by replacing chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, with congressional review procedures for agency rules. These procedures include agency reports to each House of Congress and the Comptroller General before a rule takes effect, a joint resolution of approval procedure for major rules, and provisions on judicial review and private rights of action.

  (Under the Speaker's announced policy of January 3, 2025, Mr.

  Mr. SCHWEIKERT. Mr
items.summary: Rep. Schweikert, recognized for 60 minutes as the designee of the majority leader, delivered a floor speech on federal spending, debt, and interest costs. The speech cites figures including baseline spending of $86 trillion over 10 years, interest reaching 30 percent of tax receipts by 2034, and an 11 percent Medicare trust fund reduction projected for 2033 in the Social Security and Medicare actuary report. It also discusses Congressional Budget Office scoring, a Joint Economic Committee estimate of obesity-related healthcare spending, and proposed tax increases.
items.title: STOP BATHING IN FOLKLORE AND START BATHING IN MATH

  (Under the Speaker's announced policy of January 3, 2025, Mr.
Davidson of Ohio was recognized for 30 minutes.)

                             General Leave

  Mr. DAVIDSON. Mr. Speaker, I
items.summary: Rep. Davidson, recognized for 30 minutes, delivered a special order on central bank digital currencies (CBDCs), defining them and describing their relationship to the Federal Reserve and the Bank for International Settlements. The speech states that more than 100 countries are developing CBDCs, describes the digital identity and transaction-data components of China's system, and references the Bank Secrecy Act and know-your-customer requirements. The speech opposes the development of a U.S. CBDC and calls for protections of transaction privacy.
items.title: CENTRAL BANK DIGITAL CURRENCY

items.summary: At the request of Senator Sullivan, the Senate Record printed GAO decision B-337200, dated June 25, 2025, on whether the Bureau of Land Management's Central Yukon Record of Decision and Approved Resource Management Plan is a rule under the Congressional Review Act. GAO concludes that the Central Yukon RMP meets the APA definition of a rule, that none of the three CRA exceptions applies, and that it is therefore subject to CRA review. items.summary: Senator Shaheen submitted amendment SA 2561 to H.R. 1 (as modified by SA 2360), proposing to strike section 70523 and insert new Public Health Service Act section 2799A-11, with parallel provisions in ERISA section 726 and Internal Revenue Code section 9826. The provisions require group health plans and health insurance issuers to cover selected insulin products without a deductible for plan years beginning on or after January 1, 2026, and to limit cost-sharing to $35 per 30-day supply, or from 2027 to the lesser of $35 or 25 percent of the net negotiated price. The amendment also applies the insulin requirements to qualified health plans and catastrophic plans under Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act section 1302, and it was ordered to lie on the table.

items.summary: Senator Booker submitted amendment SA 2598 to H.R. 1 (as modified by SA 2360), proposing a new Chapter 7 titled "Respect, Advancement, and Increasing Support for Educators Act of 2025" or the "RAISE Act of 2025". The chapter adds Internal Revenue Code section 36C, a teacher tax credit of $1,000 for eligible educators plus an applicable amount of up to $14,000 ($9,000 for early childhood educators without a bachelor's degree) scaled by the student poverty ratio of qualifying schools above 39 percent, with inflation adjustments for taxable years beginning after 2026. The chapter also directs the Secretary of Education to collect school information, prohibits reducing teacher pay or teacher loan forgiveness because of the credit, and sets limitations on employers that engage in collective bargaining, and it was ordered to lie on the table.

items.summary: The House resolved into the Committee of the Whole to consider H.R. 3944, the Military Construction, Veterans Affairs, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2026, which provides appropriations for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026. Chair Alford described the bill as including nearly $18 billion for military construction and full funding for veterans' healthcare and benefits, while Ranking Member Wasserman Schultz stated opposition, citing increased community care funding, reduced funding for military construction relative to the President's request, and several riders. General debate was allotted one hour, equally divided.

items.summary: Mrs. Ramirez of Illinois, designated by the minority leader, delivered a 60-minute Special Order titled Holding Power Accountable. The speaker described a visit by four Members of Congress to the ICE Processing Center in Broadview, Illinois, stated that the Members were denied entry or access, and cited section 527(a) of Public Law 118-47 regarding congressional access to Department of Homeland Security facilities. Other Members, including Mr. Carter of Louisiana and Mrs. Watson Coleman, also spoke on congressional oversight of the executive branch and on ICE facility access.

NO TAX DOLLARS FOR TERRORISTS ACT

  Mr. BURCHETT. Mr. Speaker, I move to suspend the rules and pass the
bill (H.R. 260) to require a strategy to oppose financial or material
support by foreign countries and nongovernment
items.summary: The House considered H.R. 260, the 'No Tax Dollars for Terrorists Act,' on a motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill as amended, with 20 minutes of debate allotted to each side. The bill requires the Secretary of State to report within 180 days on foreign assistance to the Taliban and to develop a strategy to discourage such assistance, and it requires further reports on Afghan direct cash assistance, the Afghan Fund, and the Haqqani Network bounty on specified schedules. The debate excerpt is truncated.
items.title: NO TAX DOLLARS FOR TERRORISTS ACT

items.opening_verbatim:
SANCTION SEA PIRATES ACT OF 2025

  Mr. BURCHETT. Mr. Speaker, I move to suspend the rules and pass the
bill (H.R. 1998) to require the imposition of sanctions with respect to
foreign persons engaged in piracy, and for o
items.summary: Mr. Burchett moved to suspend the rules and pass H.R. 1998, the Sanction Sea Pirates Act of 2025, as amended. The bill directs the President to impose asset-blocking and visa sanctions on foreign persons the President determines knowingly engage in piracy, defined by reference to chapter 81 of title 18, United States Code. It includes exceptions for certain humanitarian, intelligence, law enforcement, and national security activities, a presidential waiver certified to Congress, and a sense of Congress section on combating piracy off Somalia and in the Gulf of Aden.
items.title: SANCTION SEA PIRATES ACT OF 2025

items.opening_verbatim:
ASSESSMENT OF TRANS-ATLANTIC SUBMARINE FIBER OPTIC CABLE

  Mr. BILIRAKIS. Mr. Speaker, I move to suspend the rules and pass the
bill (H.R. 1737) to direct the Secretary of Commerce to submit to
Congress a report containing an asses
items.summary: Mr. Bilirakis moved to suspend the rules and pass H.R. 1737, which directs the Secretary of Commerce to submit a report to Congress within one year of enactment. The report would assess the value, cost, and feasibility of a trans-Atlantic submarine fiber optic cable connecting the contiguous United States, the United States Virgin Islands, Ghana, and Nigeria. Required elements include the lifespan and security of existing cables linking the Virgin Islands to the contiguous United States, telecommunications readiness in the Virgin Islands, and the feasibility of a data center and high-security cloud facility there for specified military and national security communications.
items.title: ASSESSMENT OF TRANS-ATLANTIC SUBMARINE FIBER OPTIC CABLE

items.opening_verbatim:
ROMANCE SCAM PREVENTION ACT

  Mr. BILIRAKIS. Mr. Speaker, I move to suspend the rules and pass the
bill (H.R. 2481) to require online dating service providers to provide
fraud ban notifications to online dating servic
items.summary: Mr. Bilirakis moved to suspend the rules and pass H.R. 2481, the Romance Scam Prevention Act, which requires online dating service providers to send a fraud ban notification to any member who received a message from a banned member. Notifications must include the banned member's identifier, a statement that the banned member may be using a false identity or attempting fraud, a warning not to send cash or personal financial information, best-practice information, and customer service contact details, and must generally be provided within 24 hours of a fraud ban, with delays permitted in specified circumstances. The bill assigns enforcement to the Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general, preempts conflicting state notification requirements, and takes effect one year after enactment.
items.title: ROMANCE SCAM PREVENTION ACT

items.opening_verbatim:
GLOBAL INVESTMENT IN AMERICAN JOBS ACT OF 2025

  Mr. BILIRAKIS. Mr. Speaker, I move to suspend the rules and pass the
bill (H.R. 1679) to direct the Secretary of Commerce, in coordination
with the heads of other relevant Feder
items.summary: Mr. Bilirakis moved to suspend the rules and pass H.R. 1679, the Global Investment in American Jobs Act of 2025, which directs the Secretary of Commerce and the Comptroller General of the Government Accountability Office to conduct an interagency review of United States competitiveness in attracting foreign direct investment from responsible private-sector entities based in trusted countries. The enumerated review topics include the economic impact of such investment, data localization and intellectual property barriers, and investments by State-owned or State-backed enterprises, including entities influenced by the Chinese Communist Party. The bill requires Federal Register notice and public comment, a report to Congress within one year of enactment, and excludes laws and policies relating to the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States from the review.
items.title: GLOBAL INVESTMENT IN AMERICAN JOBS ACT OF 2025

items.opening_verbatim:
WASTEWATER INFRASTRUCTURE POLLUTION PREVENTION AND ENVIRONMENTAL SAFETY
                                  ACT

  Mr. BILIRAKIS. Mr. Speaker, I move to suspend the rules and pass the
bill (H.R. 2269) to require certain products to be labeled
items.summary: Mr. Bilirakis moved to suspend the rules and pass H.R. 2269, the Wastewater Infrastructure Pollution Prevention and Environmental Safety Act (WIPPES Act), which requires covered entities to label certain premoistened nonwoven wipes with the 'Do Not Flush' phrase and symbol. Covered products include wipes marketed as baby or diapering wipes and household or personal care wipes composed partly or entirely of petrochemical-derived fibers that have significant potential to be flushed, and the bill sets placement, size, and contrast requirements while prohibiting representations that such products can or should be flushed. The Federal Trade Commission enforces the requirements, the bill preempts non-identical state labeling requirements, and it takes effect one year after enactment.
items.title: WASTEWATER INFRASTRUCTURE POLLUTION PREVENTION AND ENVIRONMENTAL SAFETY ACT

  Mr. BILIRAKIS. Mr. Speaker, I move to suspend the rules and pass the
bill (H.R. 1664) to direct the Secretary of Commerce to take actions
necessary and appropriate to promote the
items.summary: Mr. Bilirakis moved to suspend the rules and pass H.R. 1664, the Deploying American Blockchains Act of 2025, as amended, which directs the Secretary of Commerce to serve as principal advisor to the President on policy concerning blockchain technology, other distributed ledger technology, tokens, and tokenization. The bill directs the Secretary to develop policies and best practices, establish a Blockchain Deployment Program in the Department of Commerce, examine Federal agency use and security of these technologies, and, within 180 days of enactment, establish advisory committees with specified federal and nongovernmental members. It also defines blockchain technology or other distributed ledger technology, token, and tokenization.

CHARLOTTE WOODWARD ORGAN TRANSPLANT DISCRIMINATION PREVENTION ACT

  Mr. BILIRAKIS. Mr. Speaker, I move to suspend the rules and pass the
bill (H.R. 1520) to prohibit discrimination on the basis of mental or
physical disability in cases
items.summary: The House considered H.R. 1520, the Charlotte Woodward Organ Transplant Discrimination Prevention Act, under a motion to suspend the rules and pass it. The bill prohibits a covered entity from determining that a qualified individual is ineligible for, denying, refusing to refer for, or refusing to place on a waiting list for an organ transplant or related services solely on the basis of disability, with an exception for disabilities that a physician finds medically significant after an individualized evaluation. It directs complaints to the HHS Office for Civil Rights and provides that it does not limit remedies under the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990.
items.title: CHARLOTTE WOODWARD ORGAN TRANSPLANT DISCRIMINATION PREVENTION ACT

items.opening_verbatim:
SHANDRA EISENGA HUMAN CELL AND TISSUE PRODUCT SAFETY ACT

  Mr. BILIRAKIS. Mr. Speaker, I move to suspend the rules and pass the
bill (H.R. 1082) to require the Secretary of Health and Human Services
to conduct a national, evidence-
items.summary: The House considered H.R. 1082, the Shandra Eisenga Human Cell and Tissue Product Safety Act, under a motion to suspend the rules and pass it. The bill directs the HHS Secretary to support educational materials on organ, tissue, and eye donation, and amends section 368 of the Public Health Service Act to authorize civil penalties of $20,000 per violation, daily penalties after written notice, and an amount equal to the retail value of the affected products, with a total cap of $10,000,000 per proceeding. It also requires FDA to publish information on its Tissue Reference Group, establishment registrations and inspections, requires a public docket within 60 days of enactment, and requires a report to Congress by September 30, 2026.
items.title: SHANDRA EISENGA HUMAN CELL AND TISSUE PRODUCT SAFETY ACT

  Mrs. WAGNER. Mr. Speaker, I move to suspend the rules and pass the

equitable treatment of Taiwan at the intern
items.summary: The House considered H.R. 910, the Taiwan Non-Discrimination Act of 2025, under a motion to suspend the rules and pass it, as amended. The bill directs the U.S. Governor of the International Monetary Fund to use the U.S. voice and vote to support Taiwan's admission to the Fund, its participation in IMF surveillance activities, employment opportunities for Taiwan nationals, and access to technical assistance, and states that it is U.S. policy not to discourage Taiwan from seeking membership. The Treasury Secretary may waive these requirements for up to one year at a time upon reporting to Congress, and the section ceases to have effect upon IMF approval of Taiwan's admission or 10 years after enactment.
items.title: TAIWAN NON-DISCRIMINATION ACT OF 2025

items.summary: The House considered H.R. 3394, the Fair Investment Opportunities for Professional Experts Act, under a motion to suspend the rules and pass it, as amended. The bill amends Section 2(a)(15) of the Securities Act of 1933 to add categories of accredited investors, including natural persons with individual net worth over $1,000,000 (excluding the primary residence) or income over $200,000 (or $300,000 jointly), certain licensed brokers and investment advisers, and persons with demonstrable education or job experience verified by a self-regulatory organization. It directs the Securities and Exchange Commission to revise the accredited investor definition under Regulation D within 180 days of enactment.

items.summary: Pages S3173-S3174 print the text of amendments SA 2278 through SA 2283 to S. 1582, the GENIUS Act, as submitted in the Senate on June 2, 2025. SA 2278 (Bennet) would define 'senior executive branch official' to include the President and Vice President; SA 2279 (Kennedy) would set Consumer Financial Protection Bureau employee pay under the General Schedule; and SA 2280 (Kennedy) would repeal section 704B of the Equal Credit Opportunity Act and section 1071 of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act. SA 2281 (Shaheen, Kaine, Welch, and Wyden) would exclude from International Emergency Economic Powers Act section 203 the authority to impose or increase duties or impose tariff-rate quotas; SA 2282 (Shaheen) would modify implementation of the Women, Peace, and Security Act of 2017; and SA 2283 (Shaheen) would add Title II, the 'Western Balkans Democracy and Prosperity Act.'

items.summary: Senator Shaheen submitted amendment SA 2284 to S. 1582, a bill to provide for the regulation of payment stablecoins, and the amendment was ordered to lie on the table. The amendment adds Title II, the Mobilizing and Enhancing Georgia's Options for Building Accountability, Resilience, and Independence Act, which contains definitions, sense-of-Congress statements, and statements of U.S. policy toward the Republic of Georgia. It directs the Secretary of State to submit a classified report on Russian intelligence assets in Georgia within 180 days and a five-year bilateral strategy within 90 days, and it directs the President to determine within 90 days whether specified foreign persons have engaged in significant corruption or acts of violence or intimidation, with related inadmissibility and sanctions provisions.

253RD ANNIVERSARY OF THE ``GASPEE'' RAID

  Mr. WHITEHOUSE. Mr. President, I take the Senate back to June 9 of
1772, and I read from Rory Raven's ``Burning the Gaspee.''

       A handful of longboats glided across the water
items.summary: Senator Whitehouse delivered remarks marking the 253rd anniversary of the Gaspee raid, recounting the June 1772 burning of the British naval schooner HMS Gaspee off the coast of Rhode Island. The remarks draw on Rory Raven's 'Burning the Gaspee' and Nick Bunker's 'An Empire on the Edge,' and the Senator requested that a December 14, 2023 Washington Post article on the Gaspee affair be printed in the Record. The article states that the Gaspee was burned in June 1772, about eighteen months before the Boston Tea Party, and that the British Crown offered a bounty for the participants, though no one came forward to provide information.
items.title: 253RD ANNIVERSARY OF THE "GASPEE" RAID

respect to the scheduling of fentanyl-related
items.summary: S. 331, the Halt All Lethal Trafficking of Fentanyl Act, was called up in the House under House Resolution 489 for immediate consideration. The bill amends the Controlled Substances Act to place in schedule I any material containing a fentanyl-related substance, defined by specified structural modifications to fentanyl, and creates an alternative registration process for schedule I research. The text also directs the Department of Justice Inspector General to complete a study on research involving fentanyl within one year of enactment.

items.summary: H.R. 2056, the District of Columbia Federal Immigration Compliance Act of 2025, was called up in the House under House Resolution 489, with an amendment in the nature of a substitute from the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform. As amended, the bill provides that the District of Columbia may not have in effect any statute, ordinance, policy, or practice that prohibits or restricts District entities or officials from sharing citizenship or immigration status information or from complying with lawful Department of Homeland Security detainer requests under sections 236 or 287 of the Immigration and Nationality Act. items.summary: Senator Merkley stated that the GENIUS Act, which sets rules for payment stablecoins, contains no guardrails addressing conduct by the President, the Vice President, or other officials, and he objected to the majority leader's decision not to permit amendment votes. He cited the sale of the President's meme coin and a $2 billion stablecoin-related investment as examples, and he urged colleagues to support amendments on these issues. Senator Gillibrand stated her support for the Hagerty-Gillibrand substitute amendment to the GENIUS Act, which would regulate stablecoins, and said that financial regulators of both administrations had asked Congress to pass such rules.

items.summary: H.R. 9608, the Less Bureaucracy, Better Family Engagement Act, was introduced July 9, 2026 by Mrs. Miller of Illinois, reported with an amendment on November 17, 2026 (Report No. 119-879), and referred to the Committee of the Whole House on the State of the Union. The bill would transfer to the Secretary of Health and Human Services the functions the Secretary of Education exercises under four programs: Family Engagement in Education Programs under part E of title IV of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965, the Community Support for School Success program, the National Activities for School Safety program, and the Ready to Learn Programming Grant program. The bill also transfers related personnel, assets, contracts, and unexpended appropriations; directs the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to ensure no net increase in full-time equivalent employees and to certify compliance; and sets out savings provisions for existing legal documents, pending proceedings, and suits, with the transfers taking effect six months after enactment and early implementation permitted before that date.
items.title: 119 HR 9608 RH: Less Bureaucracy, Better Family Engagement Act

items.summary: H.R. 4464, the Preventive Health Savings Act, introduced July 16, 2025 by Mr. Obernolte and reported to the House on November 17, 2026, amends Section 202 of the Congressional Budget and Impoundment Control Act of 1974 by adding subsection (h). Upon request by the budget and primary-jurisdiction committee leaders, the Director of the Congressional Budget Office must determine whether proposed legislation would produce net reductions in budget outlays in the budgetary outyears through preventive health care, and must include a description and estimate of any such reductions in projections on that legislation. Any such estimate is a supplementary estimate and may not be used to determine compliance with the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 or other budgetary enforcement controls.
items.title: 119 HR 4464 RH: Preventive Health Savings Act

items.summary: H.R. 5525, the Stop DC Capital Authoritarian Motorvehicle Enforcement and Restoration of Autonomy Act, introduced September 19, 2025 by Mr. Perry and reported with an amendment on November 17, 2026, repeals Title IX of the Fiscal Year 1997 Budget Support Act of 1996 and Section 103 of the Safety-Based Traffic Enforcement Amendment Act of 2012, which govern the District of Columbia's use of automated traffic enforcement systems. The bill also repeals Section 9e of the District of Columbia Traffic Act, 1925, which governs signage prohibiting certain right turns at red traffic signals. The bill's short title also permits citation as the Stop DC CAMERA Act.
items.title: 119 HR 5525 RH: Stop DC Capital Authoritarian Motorvehicle Enforcement and Restoration of Autonomy Act

items.opening_verbatim: IB Union Calendar No. 779 119th CONGRESS 2d Session H. R. 8801 [Report No. 119–884] IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES May 13, 2026 Mr. Perry introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform
items.summary: H.R. 8801, the DC Rejecting Oppressive Automotive Driving Surcharges Act, introduced May 13, 2026 by Mr. Perry and reported with an amendment on November 17, 2026, prohibits the Council of the District of Columbia from enacting, and the Mayor from enforcing, any act, resolution, or requirement that imposes a congestion toll. The bill amends Section 602(a) of the District of Columbia Home Rule Act to add enacting such a congestion toll to the list of prohibited actions. It defines a congestion toll as any charge for entry into or passing through a congestion tolling zone, and defines that zone as roadways, bridges, tunnels, approaches, or ramps located within or entering the District of Columbia.
items.title: 119 HR 8801 RH: DC Rejecting Oppressive Automotive Driving Surcharges Act

items.opening_verbatim: IB Union Calendar No. 776 119th CONGRESS 2d Session H. R. 9607 [Report No. 119–880] IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES July 9, 2026 Mr. Walberg introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce Novem
items.summary: H.R. 9607, the Less Bureaucracy, Better Workforce Development Act, introduced July 9, 2026 by Mr. Walberg and reported with an amendment on November 17, 2026, transfers to the Secretary of Labor, acting through the Assistant Secretary of Labor for Employment and Training, the functions of the Department of Education's Office of Career, Technical, and Adult Education. The transferred functions include those under the Carl D. Perkins Career and Technical Education Act of 2006 (other than sections 116 and 117) and Title II of the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act, along with adult education and related programs. The bill directs the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to ensure no net increase in full-time equivalent employees at affected agencies, sets an effective date six months after enactment with early implementation permitted, and includes savings, suit-continuation, and reference-conforming provisions.
items.title: 119 HR 9607 RH: Less Bureaucracy, Better Workforce Development Act

items.summary: The Copyright Office is publishing a final rule establishing adjusted fees for registration, recordation, record retrieval, search and certification, the Licensing Section services, and other services. The Office last adjusted fees in 2020, based on a study of our fiscal 2016 and 2017 costs. Since that time, the costs of providing Office services have risen substantially due to inflation and other increases. The adjusted fees are intended to enable recovery of a percentage of the Office's costs, closer to historical levels, without imposing undue barriers to access its services. This rule will take effect January 5, 2027.

items.summary: In September 2023, the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC or Commission) issued a safety standard for button cell or coin batteries and consumer products containing such products in accordance with Reese's Law. The standard incorporated by reference ANSI/UL 4200A-2023, Standard for Safety for Products Incorporating Button Batteries or Coin Cell Batteries. UL Standards and Engagement (ULSE) has now issued a revised standard, ANSI/UL 4200A-2026. Consistent with Reese's Law, this direct final rule updates the mandatory safety standard to incorporate by reference ANSI/UL 4200A-2026.

items.summary: NMFS has received a request from the U.S. Department of the Navy (including the U.S. Navy and the U.S. Marine Corps; Navy) and on behalf of the U.S. Coast Guard (Coast Guard), U.S. Army (Army), and U.S. Air Force (Air Force) (hereafter, Navy, Coast Guard, Army, and Air Force are collectively referred to as the Action Proponents) for Incidental Take Regulations (ITR) and an associated Letter of Authorization (LOA) pursuant to the Marine Mammal Protection Act (MMPA). The requested regulations would govern the authorization of take of marine mammals incidental to training and testing activities and modernization and sustainment of ranges conducted in the Mariana Islands Training and Testing (MITT) Study Area over the course of 7 years from July 2027 through July 2034. NMFS requests comments on this proposed rule. NMFS will consider public comments prior to making any final decision on the promulgation of the requested ITR and issuance of the LOA; agency responses to public comments will be summarized in the final rule, if issued. items.summary: The Coast Guard is establishing a temporary safety zone for navigable waters on the Mississippi River near New Orleans, LA. The safety zone is needed to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment from potential hazards associated with the response to a vessel collision and sinking. Entry of vessels or persons into this zone is prohibited unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port, Sector New Orleans, or their designated representative.

items.opening_verbatim: FEDERAL RESERVE SYSTEM 12 CFR Part 204 [Regulation D; Docket No. R-1904] RIN 7100-AH34 Reserve Requirements of Depository Institutions AGENCY: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. ACTION: Final rule. SUMMARY: The Board is amend
items.summary: The Board is amending Regulation D, Reserve Requirements of Depository Institutions, to reflect the annual indexing of the reserve requirement exemption amount and the low reserve tranche for 2027. The annual indexation of these amounts is required notwithstanding the Board's action in March 2020 of setting all reserve requirement ratios to zero. The reserve requirement exemption amount for 2027 will remain $39.2 million, unchanged from 2026, consistent with the Federal Reserve Act (the “Act”). The Board is amending Regulation D to set the amount of the low reserve tranche at $688.5 million (increased from $674.1 million in 2026). The adjustment to the low reserve tranche is derived using a statutory formula specified in the Act. The annual indexation of the reserve requirement exemption amount and low reserve tranche is required by statute but will not affect depository institutions' reserve requirements, which will remain zero.
items.title: Reserve Requirements of Depository Institutions

items.summary: This document gives notice of a proposed class prohibited transaction exemption (PTE). This proposed QROAD class PTE (Proposed QROAD Class Exemption) would allow certain qualified professional asset managers (QPAMs) to continue relying on PTE 84-14, known as the QPAM Class Exemption, even after an event that would otherwise make them ineligible under Section I(g) of that exemption. To use this alternative path, the QPAM must comply with the protective conditions in this Proposed QROAD Class Exemption, if granted. This proposal does not change any fiduciary duties under ERISA section 404 or expand the relief available under the QPAM Class Exemption.

items.summary: NMFS is prohibiting retention of Western and Central North Pacific Ocean (WCNPO) striped marlin ( Kajikia audax ) by vessels registered for use under a Hawaii longline limited access permit for the remainder of 2026 because the longline fishery has reached the 2026 longline retention limit. WCNPO stiped marlin are those caught in the Pacific Ocean north of the Equator (0° latitude) and west of 150° W longitude. This prohibition is intended to prevent the U.S. catch limit for WCNPO striped marlin from being exceeded and ensure compliance with NMFS regulations that implement decisions of the Western and Central Pacific Fisheries Commission (WCPFC).
items.title: Pacific Island Fisheries; Longline Retention Prohibition; Striped Marlin in the Western and Central Pacific Ocean North of the Equator

items.opening_verbatim: ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY 40 CFR Part 52 [EPA-R03-OAR-2026-0661; FRL-10281-01-R3] Air Plan Approval; Virginia; Interstate Transport Requirements for the 2010 SO 2 NAAQS AGENCY: Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). ACTION: Proposed r
items.summary: Pursuant to the Federal Clean Air Act (CAA or Act), the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing to approve a State implementation plan (SIP) revision submitted by the Commonwealth of Virginia demonstrating that Virginia satisfies the interstate transport requirements of the CAA, for the 2010 1-hour sulfur dioxide (SO 2 ) primary national ambient air quality standard (NAAQS). Specifically, the EPA proposes to find that the Virginia SIP contains adequate provisions prohibiting emissions from Commonwealth sources from contributing significantly to nonattainment or interfering with maintenance of the 2010 SO 2 NAAQS in any other State, consistent with the good neighbor provision of the CAA.
items.title: Air Plan Approval; Virginia; Interstate Transport Requirements for the 2010 SO 2 NAAQS

items.summary: This document sets forth final regulations that provide guidance with respect to the automatic enrollment requirements that apply to certain retirement plans. The regulations reflect statutory changes made by the SECURE 2.0 Act of 2022 requiring that certain cash or deferred arrangements and salary reduction agreements be eligible automatic contribution arrangements that satisfy additional specified requirements. The regulations affect participants in, beneficiaries of, employers maintaining, and administrators of certain retirement plans that include cash or deferred arrangements or annuity contracts purchased under salary reduction agreements and other retirement plans that include eligible automatic contribution arrangements.

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF THE TREASURY Internal Revenue Service 26 CFR Part 1 [REG-119986-25] RIN 1545-BS05 Racial Nondiscrimination in Private Schools; Hearing AGENCY: Internal Revenue Service (IRS), Treasury. ACTION: Notice of proposed rulemaking; no
items.summary: This document provides a notice of an additional date for the public hearing on the notice of proposed rulemaking (REG-119986-25) published in the Federal Register on Friday, September 4, 2026. The proposed regulations would provide that a private school is not described as an organization exempt from Federal income tax if it discriminates on the basis of race, color, or national or ethnic origin in administration of its educational, admissions, scholarship, athletic, or other policies, based on the fundamental public policy of the United States against such practices.
items.title: Racial Nondiscrimination in Private Schools; Hearing
